flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.q: Optimistic rollup trust assumption and window?
flashcards.a: Safety needs 1-of-N honest verifiers watching assertions; ~7-day fraud window = max detection+dispute time. Unchallenged assertion finalizes; valid fraud proof slashes operator bond. BoLD (Arbitrum, Feb 2025) made challenges permissionless.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: Bisection: parties submit intermediate state roots at halved computation ranges until disagreeing on ONE step; on-chain mini-interpreter re-executes that step and declares winner. O(log steps) L1 work - the trick making optimistic verification cheap.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: Validity proof per batch verified by L1 math: 0-of-N trust (no honest-watcher need), finality minutes-hours, no exit window. Costs: prover infrastructure; zkEVM types 2-4 trade EVM compatibility for proving speed. Optimistic: cheaper ops, native EVM, slow exits.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: Type 1 fully Ethereum-equivalent (slowest) -> Type 2 EVM-equivalent -> Type 2.5 gas tweaks -> Type 3 partial precompiles -> Type 4 language-level compilation (fastest, breaks bytecode tooling). Vitalik's spectrum: compatibility vs prover cost.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: 128 KiB each; own fee market; pruned ~18 days (4096 epochs). Targets/maxes: 3/6 Dencun -> 6/9 Pectra (5/2025) -> 10/15 BPO1 (12/2025) -> 14/21 BPO2 (1/2026). PeerDAS gives ~8x headroom toward 48.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: EIP-7594: blobs erasure-coded into 128 columns; nodes custody a subset and randomly sample others - successful samples statistically imply full data availability. Per-node load stays bounded while capacity scales ~8x.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.q: Why is data availability THE bottleneck?
flashcards.a: Execution scales horizontally but consensus requires every validator to hold the bytes guaranteeing rollup safety - bandwidth/storage bound what the network can promise. Blobs exist to sell that space separately from permanent state.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: 2022: $2B+ across 13 bridges (Chainalysis). Ronin $624M (5-of-9 keys phished, Lazarus); Wormhole $325M (forged guardian signatures, Jump recapitalized); Nomad $190M (zero-proof init bug); Harmony $100M (2-of-5). Lesson: committees and sig-checks are the weak layer.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.q: Bridge design ranking by trust minimization?
flashcards.a: Native burn-mint (CCTP) > light-client/ZK-consensus verification (IBC, Rainbow, Polymer-class) > oracle networks > committees/multisigs. Ask: who can steal everything and how many must collude?

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: Stage 0 training wheels (operators can override proofs/upgrades); Stage 1 permissionless proofs + security council intervention under defined conditions; Stage 2 no-trust (invalid states can't finalize; user exits guaranteed even against keys). Most majors sat at Stage 1 through 2025.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.q: Sequencer outage: what happens to funds?
flashcards.a: Nothing - sequencing controls ordering/availability, not custody. Forced-inclusion via L1 inbox preserves escape hatches; Base outages (Sept 2023) froze UX not funds. Real risk is fairness: MEV extraction and censorship.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: Validium: DA off-chain behind committee - near-zero fees, freezing risk if committee withholds (availability not integrity). Rollup: DA on Ethereum, trust-minimized. Volition: per-account choice. Exchange-internal products tolerate validium; market-facing default rollup.

flashcards.topic: Rollups (Optimistic vs ZK), Data Availability, Bridges and Their Failures
flashcards.a: User signs desired outcome ('X USDC on chain B'); competing fillers deliver instantly from inventory and settle via the bridge later (Dutch auctions). UX instant; trust shifts to filler solvency + settlement honesty. User exposure caps at trade size, not bridge TVL.
